asset_specifications.power_curve_characteristics: Cubic rise (P ~ v^2.8) between 3.0 and 11.5 m/s, flat plateau at 100.8 MW between 11.5 and 25.0 m/s

regulatory_framework.regulation_name: MERC (Forecasting, Scheduling and Deviation Settlement for Solar and Wind Generation) Regulations

mechanics.over_forecast_rule: If Schedule > Actual + 10.08 MW, generator pays DSM penalty on excess deviation (Schedule - Actual - 10.08 MW)
mechanics.under_forecast_rule: If Schedule < Actual - 10.08 MW, generator pays DSM penalty on shortfall deviation (Actual - Schedule - 10.08 MW)
mechanics.symmetric_penalty: Both over-predicting and under-predicting beyond 10.08 MW trigger financial penalties.
mechanics.calculation_formula: Penalty (INR) = Deviation_MW * 1000 kW/MW * 0.25 hours * Rs 3.275/kWh * Slab_Multiplier

regulatory_framework.scheduler_directive: Maintain schedule strictly within Actual ± 10.08 MW. Never over-cut forecast to create shortfall penalty; never inflate forecast to create excess penalty.

regime_1_nocturnal_low_level_jet.meteorological_driver: Deccan Plateau nocturnal boundary layer stabilization and Low-Level Jet (LLJ)
regime_1_nocturnal_low_level_jet.generation_behavior: Strong, continuous, steady nocturnal generation. Night is prime power generation period.
regime_1_nocturnal_low_level_jet.scheduling_rule: NEVER set night blocks to 0.0 MW. Keep schedule anchored to 55-90 MW based on NWP hub-height winds.

regime_2_morning_breakdown.meteorological_driver: Solar sunrise and initial boundary layer convective mixing eroding the nocturnal inversion
regime_2_morning_breakdown.generation_range_mw: Steep decay from ~70 MW down to ~15 MW
regime_2_morning_breakdown.generation_behavior: Rapid downward ramp as surface warming decouples the nocturnal jet.
regime_2_morning_breakdown.scheduling_rule: Track downward ramp step-by-step. Do not lag the decay to prevent severe over-forecasting penalties.

regime_3_daytime_thermal_lull.meteorological_driver: Intense solar heating, deep turbulent boundary layer friction dissipating wind velocity
regime_3_daytime_thermal_lull.generation_range_mw: 0.5 to 7.0 MW (with calm periods near 0 MW and auxiliary power draw -100 to -350 kW)
regime_3_daytime_thermal_lull.generation_behavior: Low generation floor throughout daylight hours.
regime_3_daytime_thermal_lull.scheduling_rule: Keep schedule tight between 1.0 and 5.0 MW during midday calm. Never predict phantom daytime wind surges unless confirmed by multiple NWPs.

regime_4_evening_transition_ramp.meteorological_driver: Ground radiative cooling, thermal boundary layer collapse, and sudden onset of nocturnal LLJ
regime_4_evening_transition_ramp.generation_range_mw: Violent upward surge jumping from ~4.0 MW to >65.0 MW within 30 to 45 minutes
regime_4_evening_transition_ramp.scheduling_rule: CRITICAL RISK WINDOW. Timing error of even 1-2 blocks (15-30 min) incurs massive DSM penalties (either >10 MW excess or >10 MW shortfall). Monitor 17:30-18:00 SCADA telemetry to detect exact ramp initiation.

operational_rules: Rule 1: Maharashtra MERC 10% (10.08 MW) Two-Sided Band Mandate. Zero penalty corridor is [Actual - 10.08 MW, Actual + 10.08 MW]. Avoid both excess (>+10.08 MW) and shortfall (<-10.08 MW).
Rule 2: 24-Hour Continuous Operation. Wind produces power day and night. Nighttime is peak production (50-95 MW). Solar zeroing rules strictly forbidden.
Rule 3: Vertical Wind Shear Scaling. Hub height 133.5m is significantly windier than 10m surface or 100m NWP outputs. Scale winds using Hellmann power-law alpha = 0.143.
Rule 4: Evening Ramp Timing. Anticipate the 18:15-19:30 surge. Anchor revisions to SCADA mast anemometer trends.
Rule 5: Auxiliary Consumption Awareness. Dead calm conditions may register negative generation (-0.1 to -0.35 MW) due to turbine auxiliary consumption and transformer excitation.
